diagnosis.root_cause: The router has never produced a heartbeat record (last_checkin is null and heartbeat_status is never), so management reachability or heartbeat monitoring is unestablished. Customer service itself is currently operating normally.
evidence: The subscriber ONU is online and responding, with RX power -21.9 dBm and TX power 2.34 dBm in the normal ranges.
The seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains near -22 dBm, TX remains near +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 87, and TX bias remains healthy without a rising trend.
All visible peers on EPON0/4 are online, so there is no ONU, splitter or PON-port outage.
The OLT answers ping, SNMP and subtree queries; its CPU, memory and temperature are normal, ruling out an OLT failure or health fault.
The subscriber has three sessions in 24 hours with approximately normal duration, valid RADIUS data, consistent CRM line ID and the expected VLAN 1124.
Recent traffic is present and stable, confirming that subscriber service is passing.
The only abnormal state is the router heartbeat: no check-in has ever been recorded, with last_checkin null and heartbeat_status never.
Therefore the issue is confined to router management reachability or its monitoring configuration, not the access network or subscriber data path.

remediation.action: Verify router management-plane reachability, monitoring credentials and heartbeat-agent configuration. Establish a successful check-in and confirm it persists; do not disrupt the subscriber service, since the ONU, OLT, VLAN, RADIUS authentication and traffic are all healthy.

ground_truth.root_cause: The router has no check-in record of any kind, which means it was never enrolled in heartbeat monitoring rather than that it stopped responding. Its customers are authenticated, holding long sessions and passing normal traffic.
expected_reasoning: The router's heartbeat status is 'never' with a null last_checkin
That is different from a heartbeat that went stale, which would carry a timestamp and an elapsed time
No record at all indicates the router was never enrolled in the check-in mechanism
The ONU behind it is online with RX -21.9 and TX 2.3, both normal
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are all responding normally
Sessions are active with a 683 minute mean, close to the 11.9 hour network norm
Daily traffic is steady across all seven days with no interruption
Customers on this router are being served, so there is no outage
The finding is a monitoring gap, not a network fault

expected_escalation.review_reason: Router is not enrolled in heartbeat monitoring and should be added

distractors: A null heartbeat looks worse than a stale one and invites a Disaster conclusion
A scheduled scan targeting the router frames it as the suspect
The correct answer is that nothing is wrong with the network
